The work loop

Plan → act → verify → review: the agent turns the loop, you steer

1
Plan
agree what to build
2
Act
the agent edits files
3
Verify
tests run
4
Review
you read the changes
you steer
1Plan: the agent reads the project and proposes a plan; no edits yet
2Act: edits on a separate branch — a copy of the project you can throw away
3Verify: tests, build, screenshot
4Review: you read the changes — the diff, “before → after” — and decide
Anthropic: “explore first, then plan, then code”.

The task

A good agent task says what to do, what not to touch and how to check it is done

VAGUE
Add a priority filter.
The agent decides where the filter goes, what to change and when to stop.
→
AGENT TASK
# TASK.md
Goal: filter tickets by priority
      on the /tickets page
Do not touch: database, login
Done when: the filter test
      passes, old tests too
Check: pytest -q
Review: a human reads the diff
GenAI Basics • Lesson 16 • Agentic development06 / 16
Project rules

AGENTS.md is a short project memo the agent reads at the start of every session

# AGENTS.md
## Commands
- tests: pytest -q
- run: streamlit run app.py
## Rules
- code in src/, tests in tests/
- do not touch .env or deploy/
- new libraries only
  after asking
60,000+
open-source projects already use AGENTS.md, an open format
Read by: Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Junie, Antigravity. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md if there is none.
Short and concrete: commands and limits, not an essay.

Permissions

The permission mode decides what the agent does on its own and what needs your OK

93%
of permission prompts people simply approve — they get tired of reading
~17%
of risky actions the auto check still misses (Anthropic’s test)
plan
reads and plans only
manual
asks before edits and commands
acceptEdits
edits files and runs simple file commands itself; asks for other commands
auto
a checker model reviews commands · default in the terminal
bypass
no checks — throwaway container only
← saferfaster, riskier →
GenAI Basics • Lesson 16 • Agentic development08 / 16
Verify

“If you can’t verify it, don’t ship it”: give the agent a check it can run itself

$ pytest -q
..F                               [100%]
FAILED tests/test_filter.py::
  test_filter_by_priority - TypeError: ...
1 failed, 2 passed in 0.06s
# the agent edits app.py: adds priority
$ pytest -q
...                               [100%]
3 passed in 0.02s
Real output on the homework starter project (the error is shortened).
1A test fails: first write a check for what you need
2The agent fixes: edits the code until the test passes
3All tests pass: the new one and the old ones
4You read the diff: tests don’t see everything — meaning, style, extras
The agent’s undo (Esc Esc, /rewind) reverts file edits, but not terminal commands.
The real undo button is git: each task on its own branch.

Speed

Experienced developers felt 20% faster with AI — the measurement showed 19% slower

METR, early 2025: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks in their own projects, tools of that time (Cursor + Claude 3.5/3.7).
← slowerfaster →
Expected beforehand
+24%
Felt afterwards
+20%
Measured
−19%
2026 follow-up: probably faster now, but the data is weak — people refused to work without AI.
Takeaway: feeling fast ≠ being fast. Measure on your own tasks.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 16 • Agentic development10 / 16
Incidents

An agent does whatever it can reach: keys, databases and other people’s text in the project

9 seconds
PocketOS, 2026: the agent found an access key in an unrelated file and deleted the database with its backups; per the founder, data was later restored
Code freeze
Replit, 2025: the agent deleted SaaStr’s live database although changes were frozen
2,349
secrets leaked: an infected Nx library (a ready-made module developers download) stole keys and made installed AI agents search for secret files, 2025
A key within the agent’s reach = a permission given to the agent.
Clinejection, 2026: a command in a GitHub issue title → the project’s AI bot ran it → publishing keys were stolen → an infected Cline version went out.

GenAI Basics • Lesson 16 • Agentic development12 / 16
Safe work

Six rules that sharply cut the risk of such incidents

  1. A separate branch per task
    git is your undo button
  2. No production keys nearby PocketOS
    not in the code, not in the project’s settings files
  3. Sandbox and least privilege Replit
    a closed environment; deny deleting and pushing code
  4. Other people’s text is unverified code Nx · Clinejection
    READMEs, issues, foreign AGENTS.md, skills, MCP
  5. A human reads every change
    ideally with fresh eyes or a second agent
  6. Only a human merges and ships
    Copilot’s agent can only propose changes; a human accepts them
The no-checks mode (bypass, --yolo, danger-full-access) — only in a throwaway container or virtual machine.

Homework

Homework: one small task done by an agent and checked by you

  1. The homework starter project (app.py + tests) or your own small repository
  2. AGENTS.md: commands and limits
  3. TASK.md: goal, do not touch, done when, check
  4. The agent in plan mode → edits on a separate branch
  5. Run the check yourself, save a screenshot, read the diff
  6. AGENT_EVIDENCE.md: the agent’s plan, what ran, what changed, your decision
genai-homeworks/L16/
├─ AGENTS.md
├─ TASK.md
├─ AGENT_EVIDENCE.md
└─ check.png
Don’t code? Change only the README; the check is a screenshot of the page. No production keys.
